article_notes: 15 naturally infected B. canis dogs (12 university clinic Zurich, 3 private practices), samples at first admission before any treatment. Haematology and biochemistry exclude the 3 private-practice dogs (6 vs 6); parasitaemia, hand-held lactate and glucose, CRP and SAA use all 15 (8 nonsurvivors vs 7 survivors). Table 1 shows median (min-max). The 3 experimentally infected beagles (followed to acute crisis) have no outcome groups and are not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: nonsurvivors vs survivors
severity_definitions.definition: Naturally infected B. canis dogs (Switzerland, 2011-2013) grouped by outcome: death (6 died spontaneously within 24 h of admission, 2 euthanised within 48 h for clinical deterioration) vs survival (cure confirmed by negative smear and PCR 14 days after admission).
severity_definitions.quote: The animals were categorized into 2 groups according to clinical outcome, which was defined as survival (survivor, n = 7 dogs) or death (nonsurvivor, n = 8 dogs).
severity_definitions.follow_up_horizon: 14 days (all deaths within 48 h of admission)
